intro: Some secret groups keep secrets to protect belonging. The groups in this unit kept secrets to protect harm. Around 1900, extortion gangs in New York and Chicago sent threatening letters signed with a black hand. In the 1920s, bootlegging gangs in Chicago grew rich by selling alcohol when it was against the law. Both depended on fear, bribes and silence.

This unit keeps its eyes on the people who stood up. You will meet Joseph Petrosino, a New York detective who fought extortion with records. You will meet the Italian Americans of Chicago who formed the White Hand Society. You will meet citizens who named public enemies, a scientist who studied bullets, and a tax agent who found the ledgers that tied Al Capone to his money. You will also see how an unfair stereotype hurt honest immigrant families.

By the end, you will be able to explain what extortion and organized crime are, and why silence helped them. You will sort documented facts from disputed claims and popular legends. You will explain how patient work with records and brave witnesses brought results where force had failed.
bigQuestion: How do communities break the silence that protects criminal secret groups?

timeline.t: A mob in New Orleans kills 11 Italian men taken from the jail
The name "Black Hand" is first used for extortion letters in New York
Chicago's Italian Americans propose the White Hand Society
Detective Joseph Petrosino is killed in Palermo, Sicily
Business leaders found the Chicago Crime Commission
Prohibition begins; Johnny Torrio takes over a Chicago crime group
Torrio is wounded and retires, leaving Al Capone in charge
Supreme Court rules that money from crime must be reported for tax
St. Valentine's Day Massacre; a scientific crime lab opens
The Crime Commission names 28 public enemies, Capone first
A federal jury convicts Capone of income-tax crimes

words.d: getting money from someone by threatening to hurt them or their property
sent or done without giving a name
a person who moves to a new country to live
an unfair idea that everyone in a group is the same
a person who tells what they saw or know, often in a court
to send a person out of a country, back to where they came from
the period from 1920 to 1933 when making and selling alcohol was illegal in the United States
making, moving or selling alcohol against the law
dishonest behavior by people in power, such as taking bribes
the science of guns, bullets and the marks they leave
illegally avoiding paying the taxes you owe
a book where a business records money coming in and going out

choices: One worldwide society with a single leader
A police squad in New York
A group that fought crime in Chicago
A method of extortion used by many small gangs
test.why: Arthur Woods and later historians describe the Black Hand as a method many separate gangs used.

test.q: Who were most victims of Black Hand extortion?
choices: Italian immigrants
Police officers
Bankers in Palermo
Federal tax agents
test.why: Black Hand criminals mostly targeted other Italian immigrants.

test.q: What was Joseph Petrosino trying to do when he was killed in 1909?
choices: Arrest Al Capone
Start the White Hand Society
Gather criminal records in Sicily
Study bullets under a microscope
test.why: Petrosino went to Sicily to gather criminal records so extortionists could be deported.

test.q: What was the White Hand Society?
choices: A Black Hand gang in New York
A crime lab at Northwestern
A Chicago group of Italian Americans fighting the Black Hand
A secret committee of tax agents
test.why: Chicago's Italian Americans formed the White Hand in 1907 and 1908 to fight extortion.

test.q: What does the 1891 New Orleans lynching show?
choices: The harm prejudice against Italians could cause
That the Black Hand began in New Orleans
That Petrosino worked in New Orleans
That Prohibition started early in Louisiana
test.why: A mob killed 11 Italian men. It shows how an unfair stereotype led to terrible harm.

test.q: Why did extortion gangs warn victims to tell no one?
choices: Talking about crimes was illegal
The letters were meant to be funny
They wanted to protect the police
They depended on silence to avoid being caught
test.why: Extortion works only when victims stay silent. Witnesses who speak up weaken it.

choices: A ban on immigration from Italy
A ban on making and selling alcohol, 1920 to 1933
A tax on income from crime
A law that created the Crime Commission
test.why: Prohibition made alcohol illegal from 1920 to 1933 and created a huge illegal market.

test.q: Who took over a Chicago crime group after Big Jim Colosimo was killed in 1920?
choices: Frank J. Wilson
Johnny Torrio
Eliot Ness
Robert Isham Randolph
test.why: Torrio took over in 1920, with young Al Capone working under him.

choices: Selling alcohol in a speakeasy
Keeping careful account books
Moving to a new country
Dishonest behavior by people in power, such as taking bribes
test.why: Corruption means officials acting dishonestly, such as taking gang money to ignore crimes.

test.q: Which statement about the St. Valentine's Day Massacre is disputed?
choices: That Capone ordered it
That seven men were killed
That it happened on 14 February 1929
That no one was convicted
test.why: Many believe Capone ordered it, but it was never proven. The other facts are documented.

test.q: What did Calvin Goddard contribute after the massacre?
choices: The public enemies list
The 1927 Supreme Court ruling
Ballistics work that led to a scientific crime lab
Brewery raids that cost Capone money
test.why: Goddard studied bullets and became director of the Scientific Crime Detection Laboratory.

test.q: Why did the Secret Six keep members' names secret?
choices: To hide crimes they were committing
To follow a Black Hand rule
To protect them from gangs while they fought crime
To win an election
test.why: Their anonymity protected people who stood against harm.

test.q: Which 1927 ruling opened the way to the tax case against Capone?
choices: United States v. Sullivan
Capone v. United States
United States v. Petrosino
The Eighteenth Amendment
test.why: Sullivan ruled that money from crime is income and must be reported for tax.

test.q: How did investigators connect the Hawthorne Smoke Shop ledgers to a witness?
choices: By testing the bullets from Clark Street
By reading the public enemies list
By raiding a brewery
By matching the handwriting to bank deposit slips
test.why: Handwriting on deposit slips led Frank J. Wilson's team to the bookkeeper Leslie Shumway.

test.q: Which statement about Al Capone's conviction is accurate?
choices: Eliot Ness's gunfight ended his career
He was convicted of tax crimes, not murder
He was convicted of the St. Valentine's Day Massacre
He was never convicted of any crime
test.why: In 1931 a federal jury convicted him on five tax counts. He was never convicted of murder.

write.prompt: Who did more to weaken the criminal groups in this unit: police and government agents, or ordinary community members? Make a claim. Support it with two or three facts from the unit, and explain how each one helped break the silence.
tips: Name specific people and groups, such as Petrosino, the White Hand Society, the Crime Commission or Frank J. Wilson.
Give the other side fairly before you explain your choice.
Keep documented facts separate from disputed claims and legends.
Use at least three unit words, such as extortion, witness or tax evasion.
